definition: A vendor-specific stop screen, such as the Windows blue screen or the macOS spinning wheel, shown after a fatal error from bad drivers, faulty RAM, or failing hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: The monitor shows no picture at all; check monitor power, input, and cable first, then the video card, and if the PC never completes POST, the RAM, CPU, or motherboard.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: Pressing the power button gets no response at all: no fans, lights, or beeps; check the outlet, power cord, and voltage switch, then replace the power supply.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A PC that responds slowly to everything, often because CPU, memory, or disk use stays above 80 percent, the system drive has under 10 percent free, or malware runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: Components running too hot because of failed fans, dust, blocked vents, missing slot covers, or a loose heat sink, which leads to lockups, throttling, and unexpected shutdowns.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: An odor of hot plastic or electronics, most often from a failing power supply; shut the PC down and unplug it at once, then look for melted or scorched parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: The computer turns itself off without warning, usually from overheating, a failing power supply, or new components that draw more power than the supply can deliver.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

definition: A program closes or stops responding unexpectedly; when it keeps happening across programs, suspect faulty or incompatible RAM and run a memory test.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

definition: A whine, buzz, or rattle from inside the case, usually a dusty or failing fan or a cable brushing a fan blade, since only moving parts make sound.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A failed motherboard capacitor bulges at the top and may leak electrolyte, causing random reboots and crashes; replace the board and never touch the residue.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: The firmware's built-in check of the CPU, RAM, video, and other basic hardware at startup; if it finds a fault, the boot process stops.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A pattern of short and long beeps from the system speaker that reports a startup hardware fault; meanings differ by BIOS maker, so look them up in the manual.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A diagnostic card plugged into an expansion slot or USB port that shows a two-digit code for each startup test, revealing where the boot process stops.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A handheld device that plugs into the 24-pin, CPU, SATA, and Molex connectors and shows whether the 12 V, 5 V, and 3.3 V outputs are correct.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

definition: A built-in Windows tool, started with mdsched.exe or from the recovery environment, that restarts the PC and tests the RAM for errors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

definition: Chips, memory modules, and expansion cards slowly working out of their sockets after many heating and cooling cycles, causing intermittent faults that reseating fixes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: The clock resets to a default date at each boot and other firmware settings are lost, because the CR2032 CMOS battery is drained below about 2.5 V.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 23: Troubleshooting Motherboards, CPUs, RAM, and Power

definition: A small light on a case, drive, or enclosure that shows drive activity or health; one that never blinks, stays on solid, or turns amber signals a problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A harsh scraping from a moving part: in a hard disk, a failing spindle motor or heads cutting the platter; in a printer, stripped gears or a bad stepper motor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A regular ticking from a mechanical hard disk that means it is failing; copy the data to another drive at once, before it stops working.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: The firmware finds no disk with a startup loader, caused by a loose or reversed SATA cable, a wrong boot order, a dead drive, or a damaged MBR.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: Files that will not open or contain errors, caused by failing sectors, a power surge during a write, or malware; back up what remains and test the drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A disk that takes much longer than normal to open and save files because it is nearly full, fragmented, infected, or developing bad sectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A drive that the firmware detects but File Explorer does not show, usually because it is not initialized, partitioned, or given a letter in Disk Management.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: Monitoring built into drives that records error counts and health data to warn of failure; check its status with wmic diskdrive get status.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A storage performance measure of how many reads and writes a drive completes each second; a steady drop in benchmark results points to a failing device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: An array loses more drives than its level can survive, such as one disk in RAID 0 or two in RAID 5, so the data must be restored from backup.
acceptedAnswers: Redundant array of independent disks failure
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: The system cannot find the RAID volume at all, showing errors like Array Not Found, often because a BIOS reset changed the SATA mode from RAID to AHCI.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A beeping tone or siren from a RAID controller or storage enclosure that warns of a failed drive or controller fault; check the RAID utility before silencing it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A mirrored or parity volume that still runs after one member disk failed or was removed, but has no redundancy left until the disk is replaced and rebuilt.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 24: Troubleshooting Storage Drives and RAID Arrays

definition: A blurry picture, caused on a projector by poor lens focus, and on a flat panel by an unsupported resolution, custom scaling, a bad cable, or nearby interference.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A faint permanent ghost of a static picture that stays visible over everything else, mostly on OLED and plasma panels; the usual fix is replacing the display.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A single point on a flat panel that never lights, seen as a dark dot on a white background; it cannot be repaired, so the panel is replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A single point on a flat panel that stays lit in one color on a black background; pixel-repair software, rapid color changes, or gentle pressure may free it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A picture that flickers or blinks off and on, caused by a refresh rate set too low, a failing backlight or inverter, a loose cable, or an unsupported resolution.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Colors look wrong or tinted because of a failing panel controller board, bent connector pins, or a loose cable; recalibrate with the OSD or dccw.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A picture too dark to read, caused by low brightness settings or, if no setting helps, a failing backlight that must be replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A picture that looks stretched, squashed, or trapezoid-shaped, usually because the chosen resolution has a different aspect ratio from the panel's native one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Stray blocks, lines, or garbled patterns drawn over the picture, often from an overheating video card, failing video memory, or a bad driver.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: A monitor or projector set to the wrong port in its on-screen menu, such as HDMI while the PC uses DisplayPort, so it shows a black screen with no signal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: A loose, damaged, or overlong video cable that causes flicker, fuzziness, random signal loss, or no picture; reseat it or swap in a cable rated for the distance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: A projector lamp at the end of its life, so no light comes out at all; replace it with the exact model after it cools, then reset the lamp counter.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: No sound from a monitor or TV because it is muted, Windows sends audio to the wrong output device, or a DVI cable is used, which carries video only.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A projector that turns itself off during use, nearly always from overheating; clean the air filter, check the fan, give it room to vent, and check the lamp.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Icons and text appear far too large, too small, or past the screen edges because the resolution or scaling percentage does not match the monitor's native setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: A projector setting that squares up a trapezoid-shaped picture caused by aiming the projector at an angle to the screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 25: Troubleshooting Video Issues

definition: A basic 640 × 480 display mode Windows starts in when the video driver fails or the resolution is unsupported, so the driver or setting can be fixed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: An aging battery that holds much less charge than when new, so the device runs only briefly unplugged; replace it if recalibration does not help.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A lithium battery that puffs up from overcharging, age, damage, or a defect and can crack the case; power off, unplug, and send it for recycling.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A device that charges slowly or not at all, most often because of a damaged cable, a failed adapter, or lint in the port; check the cable first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: Harm from water or other fluid getting inside a device; power it off, remove the case, SIM, and memory card, and let it dry fully before restarting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: Bent, broken, or loose charging and data connectors; they usually cannot be repaired alone, so the board or the whole device is replaced.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Cracked or shattered display glass from a drop or impact; replace the screen or the device, and use protectors and rugged cases to prevent it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: One full use of a battery's capacity from empty to 100 percent; batteries handle only several hundred of these, so phones wear out in three to five years.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: A touchscreen layer that stops registering finger or pen input because of a frozen app or OS, a loose display connector, or a damaged screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: The pointer slowly moves on its own in one direction, usually because a laptop pointing stick does not recenter; move it back and forth or recalibrate it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The process of aligning where a touchscreen registers a tap with where the image is, run in Windows from Tablet PC Settings when touches land off target.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The pointer jumps around the screen while the user types, because a palm brushes the touchpad; lower its sensitivity or disable it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A pen that no longer writes on a touchscreen because its battery is dead, its tip is worn, it is not paired, or the screen does not support it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: Apps fail to install because of low storage, an outdated OS, missing permissions, or blocked unknown sources; free space and update first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 26: Troubleshooting Mobile Devices

definition: Weak, dropping, or absent Wi-Fi, cellular, or Bluetooth links on a mobile device, often from distance or obstructions, or airplane mode left on.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A Wi-Fi link that keeps dropping and reconnecting, most often from a weak signal at the edge of range, obstructions, or too many clients on one access point.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: Transfers take far longer than normal because of network congestion, old cabling or switches, or a host with too many open connections, seen with netstat -a.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: A host can reach local resources but not other networks or the internet, often from a wrong gateway or DNS server or an APIPA address; check with ipconfig /all.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: Variation in packet delay, measured in milliseconds, so traffic arrives unevenly; it ruins voice and video calls and is reduced with QoS and wired links.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Choppy, garbled, or dropped internet phone calls caused by congestion, delay, and uneven packet arrival; fix by giving voice traffic priority with QoS.
acceptedAnswers: Poor Voice over Internet Protocol quality
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A switch link that rapidly alternates between up and down states, caused by a bad patch cable, a duplex mismatch, power-saving settings, or a faulty SFP module.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Long delay for packets to travel from source to destination, also called lag, which hurts real-time apps like gaming and video conferencing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Radio noise from microwaves, cordless phones, fluorescent lights, motors, or neighboring networks on the same channel that weakens and disrupts Wi-Fi signals.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: A user cannot log on to network resources because of wrong credentials, Caps Lock, a locked or expired account, an unreachable domain controller, or clock skew.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Access to outside websites and services keeps dropping while the LAN may work, caused by failing cables, overloaded or outdated routers, DNS errors, or ISP outages.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: A router or switch feature that prioritizes chosen traffic, such as voice calls, so it gets bandwidth first when the network is congested.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: A holding area that collects arriving voice packets and releases them at an even pace, smoothing out delay variation on VoIP calls.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Two hosts on a network use the same address, so one loses access, usually because someone set a static address inside the DHCP range.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A link where one end sends in full-duplex and the other in half-duplex, causing collisions, errors, slow transfers, and a port that goes up and down.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 12: Core Hardware and Network Troubleshooting

definition: A walk-through with a Wi-Fi analyzer that maps signal strength, SSIDs, and channels in an area, often shown as a heat map of coverage.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: A weak radio signal from too much distance to the access point or bad antenna placement; move closer, reposition the router, or upgrade the adapter.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 27: Troubleshooting Wired and Wireless Network Problems

definition: Vertical streaks on every page: white ones from a dirty transfer corona, black ones from a scratched drum or dirty charging corona, or gaps from clogged inkjet nozzles.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Pages of random symbols or nonsense text, caused by the wrong printer driver, a mismatch between PCL and PostScript, or a failing formatter board.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Output that is too light overall, usually because the toner or ink is low; shake or replace the toner cartridge, or replace the ink cartridge.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Random dots of toner or ink scattered across printed pages, usually from paper dust, label glue, or debris inside the printer, or a leaking cartridge.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A faint copy of a previous page appears on the current one, caused by a broken drum cleaning blade or bad erase lamps; try a new toner cartridge first.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Toner that rubs off when the page is touched, because the fuser is not heating and melting it into the paper; replace the fuser.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A laser printer feeds paper with nothing on it, because the toner is empty, the sealing tape is still on, or the transfer corona or high-voltage supply failed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The same smudge repeats down the page at equal spacing, matching the circumference of a dirty roller or a chipped drum; clean or replace that roller.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: Output prints in portrait when landscape was wanted, or the reverse, because the app, driver, or printer settings for page layout do not match.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

definition: Paper stuck inside the paper path, caused by obstructions, worn feed or exit rollers, damp or wrong paper, or a broken drive gear.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The printer fails to pick up any sheet from the tray, usually because the pickup rollers are worn smooth or the paper is too smooth to grip.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The printer pulls several sheets at once, caused by a worn separation pad or paper that is damp, sticky, or rough; fan or replace the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A finisher fault where bent staples block the stapling unit so sets come out unstapled; clear the jammed staples and refill the cartridge if empty.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: A finisher fault where output pages are not punched or are punched in the wrong place; check the finishing settings and clear debris from the punch unit.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting

definition: The printer does not detect an installed paper tray, from a tray not fully seated, wrong size settings on the control panel, old firmware, or a bad sensor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

definition: Several jobs wait in line without printing because the printer is offline, paused, out of paper, or one job at the front has stalled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

definition: Jobs stay stuck and cannot be canceled because a job is corrupted or the spooler failed; stop the spooler, empty the spool PRINTERS folder, and restart it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

definition: The Windows service that queues print jobs on disk and feeds them to the printer; restart it with net stop spooler and net start spooler.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers

definition: A network printer that clients cannot reach, often because its IP address changed through DHCP; give it a reservation or static address and print a configuration page.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 1 Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting
